zh.title: 德國將退役Transall C-160D改裝為空中消防機
zh.summary: TAS主導改裝兩架退役C-160D為消防機；首機註冊D-AMJT，計畫2027年消防季投入服務
body: 兩架德國空軍退役的Transall C-160D運輸機正進行改裝，準備以空中消防機身分重返服役。該改裝計畫由總部位於下薩克森邦的Total Aeronautical Services GmbH（TAS）主導，機上主貨艙將安裝儲水槽與阻燃劑噴灑設備，以執行滅火任務。
首架改裝機已獲分配民用註冊編號D-AMJT，成為德國航空史上首架獲准以民用註冊運作的C-160 Transall。德國聯邦航空局（LBA）與聯邦國防軍採購局（BAAINBw）對該計畫提供支持。據報導，改裝工程已進入後期階段，首飛前的密集準備工作正在進行中。
機上配備由澳洲消防設備公司Helitak Firefighting Equipment開發的消防系統，主貨艙水槽可容納最多14噸水或阻燃劑。水或阻燃劑透過機腹下方安裝的設備釋放，以保持接近飛機重心。該設備每秒可投放3,000公升，地面加水約需三分鐘。
TAS表示，首架飛機預計在2027年歐洲消防季前投入服務。TAS總經理Maren Reese指出，隨著歐洲野火問題逐年加劇，將經過驗證的軍用航空硬體改裝再利用的迫切性與實際效益日益重要。
Helitak本身已於2023年取得三架前德國空軍C-160D，其中一架已安裝消防系統，並於2026年3月在Toowoomba Wellcamp機場（WTB）完成完整投水示範。高翼設計的C-160D雙渦槳機因載重能力大、低速操控性佳且可於短未鋪設跑道起降，被國家主管機關視為空中消防的理想機型。

en.title: Germany Converts Retired Transall C-160Ds into Aerial Firefighting Aircraft
en.summary: TAS leads conversion of two retired Luftwaffe C-160Ds; first registered D-AMJT, due for 2027 firefighting season
body: Two retired German Air Force (Luftwaffe) Transall C-160D transport aircraft are being reconfigured as aerial firefighting platforms, six years after their retirement. The conversion project is led by Total Aeronautical Services GmbH (TAS), a Lower Saxony-based aviation company specialising in aircraft conversion.

The first converted aircraft has been allocated the civil registration D-AMJT, making it the first C-160 Transall in German aviation history authorised to operate under civil registry. Germany's Federal Aviation Office (LBA) and the Bundeswehr procurement agency (BAAINBw) are supporting the project. The conversion has reportedly reached an advanced stage, with intensive preparations for the initial test flight underway.

The aircraft are being equipped with a firefighting system developed by Australian firm Helitak Firefighting Equipment. A main deck tank can hold up to 14 tonnes of water or fire retardant, released through equipment fitted to the underside of the fuselage to keep it close to the plane's centre of gravity. The system can drop 3,000 litres per second, and the tank can be refilled on the ground in about three minutes.

TAS stated that the first of the two aircraft is due to enter service in time for the 2027 European firefighting season. TAS Managing Director Maren Reese said the urgency and practical impact of repurposing proven military aviation hardware was becoming increasingly important as the wildfire issue increases across Europe year-on-year.

Helitak acquired three former Luftwaffe C-160Ds in 2023 and has already fitted one with its firefighting system, performing a full water-drop demonstration at Toowoomba Wellcamp Airport (WTB)                                                                                                  in March 2026. The high-wing C-160D twin-turboprop is considered by national authorities as the ideal airframe for aerial firefighting due to its substantial payload capacity, low-speed handling, and ability to operate from short, unpaved airfields.
